Let Start be \((0,2)\) and Ziel be \((4,0)\). A path can use unit horizontal/vertical moves of length \(1\) and unit diagonal moves of length \(\sqrt2\).

Suppose a path uses \(d\) diagonal moves and \(s\) side moves. A diagonal can contribute at most \(1\) unit horizontally and at most \(1\) unit vertically toward the required displacement \((4,-2)\). Hence
\[
s\ge \max(0,4-d)+\max(0,2-d),
\]
so its length \(L\) satisfies
\[
L\ge d\sqrt2+\max(0,4-d)+\max(0,2-d).
\]
Checking possible \(d\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
d & \text{minimum possible length}\\ \hline
0 & 6\\
1 & 4+\sqrt2\\
2 & 2+2\sqrt2\\
3 & 1+3\sqrt2\\
d\ge4 & \ge4\sqrt2
\end{array}
\]
The smallest is \(2+2\sqrt2\), achieved by using two down-right diagonals and then two unit side steps.

Therefore the shortest path has length
\[
\boxed{\text{C }\,2+2\sqrt2}
\]
